# A Guide for Facilities

Know Your Rights If a Complaint or Other DMV Charges have been Filed Against You

Protect Your Facility License, Registration or Certification

What to do if a complaint is filed against you

The New York State Department of Motor Vehicles regulates all repair shops, inspection stations, dealers, vehicle dismantlers and other related businesses in NYS. To legally operate as such a business, you must register with DMV. Once your application is approved you will receive a certificate from DMV. A copy of the Commissioner's Regulations that pertain to your type of business may be found on the DMV web site at dmv.ny.gov [1]. They will explain your responsibilities to consumers. You must follow all consumer protection laws and regulations.

DMV advises all consumers who have a complaint against a dealer, inspection station, repair shop, or dismantler to make an attempt to resolve their complaint with the business manager. If they are not successful, they are advised to contact the DMV Consumer & Facilities Services Complaint Unit.

Protect Your Business: Keep a copy of all work orders in an easy-to-access location.

The Complaint Process

If a complaint has been filed against you, a Consumer Services Rep from DMV will contact you in an attempt to resolve this complaint. The CSR will explain the nature of the complaint and will also inform you of your rights, responsibilities, and your liability. If the complaint is not resolved with the CSR, the case will be sent to an Automotive Facilities Inspector (AFI) for a formal investigation.

Avoid costly penalties, fines, and the loss of valuable customersby responding to all DMV inquiries in a timely manner.

The AFI will conduct a formal investigation. The result may be no action, a warning letter (Notice of Investigation) placed in your file, or a formal administrative hearing before an Administrative Law Judge (ALJ). When Vehicle Safety initiates the hearing process, you may be offered the opportunity through a "hearing waiver" to admit to the charges and to either pay a specified monetary penalty and/or to accept a suspension. If the waiver is accepted, no hearing is required. If the offer is rejected, a hearing must be held.

The result of the hearing may be no action, a civil penalty, and/or a suspension or revocation of your ability to operate as a vehicle related business in NYS. You may also be offered the opportunity to pay restitution to the consumer in lieu of the fines and/or penalties, or to have the

### penalty reduced.

## The Hearing Process

You are entitled to hire an attorney and to bring that attorney to the hearing. The Department of Motor Vehicles is the petitioner is this case and the complainant may be a witness for the case.

As a result of the hearing, the ALJ may sustain some, all, or none of the charges. There may be no action, a warning, the imposition of a suspension, revocation, and/or civil penalties. If the ALJ only imposes civil penalties, in order to prevent the loss of your operating privilege, you must pay all fines and penalties. You will receive a letter from DMV shortly after the hearing. You will have 30 days from the date of the order by the judge to pay your fine or penalty.

Failure to pay any fines or penalties or to serve out your suspension will result in indefinite suspension of your business certificate and the possible assessment of a lien against your business. However, if you pay your fine and/or penalty or serve out your period of suspension, you will be back in business after complete compliance. If you are revoked, you must surrender all supplies and cease to operate.

You have the right to appeal any adverse decision. If you chose to appeal, you have 60 days from the date of the ALJs decision to file the Administrative Appeal Form [2] (AA-33A), which must be accompanied by the appropriate filing fee.

Avoid Losing Your Facility License, Registration or Certification

Your facility license, registration or certification enables you to operate in NYS. Complaints filed and charges brought against you can result in the loss of your privilege to operate as a business in NYS.

# About complaints and charges for dealer and transporter businesses

If you are looking to file a complaint against a dealer or transporter business, please report a problem with a DMV regulated automotive business [1].

### Complaint filed against you or your business

The New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) regulates all repair shops, inspection stations, dealers, vehicle dismantlers and other related businesses in NY State. To legally operate as such a business, you must register with the DMV. Once your application is approved you will receive a certificate from the DMV. You will also receive a copy of the Commissioner's Regulations that pertain to your type of business. They will explain your responsibilities to consumers. You must follow all consumer protection laws and regulations.

The DMV advises all consumers who have a complaint against a dealer, inspection station, repair shop, or dismantler to make an attempt to resolve their complaint with the business manager. If they are not successful, they are advised to contact the DMV Consumer & Facilities Services Complaint Unit.

- protect your business: keep a copy of all work orders in an easy-to-access location

### Complaint process

If a complaint has been filed against you, a Consumer Services Rep from the DMV will contact you in an attempt to resolve this complaint. The CSR will explain the nature of the complaint and will also inform you of your rights, responsibilities, and your liability. If the complaint is not resolved with the CSR, the case will be sent to an Automotive Facilities Inspector (AFI) for a formal investigation.

- avoid costly penalties, fines, and the loss of valuable customers by responding to all DMV inquiries in a timely manner

### Investigation process

The AFI will conduct a formal investigation. The result may be no action, a warning letter (Notice of Investigation) placed in your file, or a formal administrative hearing before an Administrative Law Judge (ALJ). When Vehicle Safety initiates the hearing process, you may be offered the opportunity through a "hearing waiver" to admit to the charges and to either pay a specified monetary penalty and/or to accept a suspension. If the waiver is accepted, no hearing is required. If the offer is rejected, a hearing must be held.

The result of the hearing may be no action, a civil penalty, and/or a suspension or revocation of your ability to operate as a vehicle related business in New York State. You may also be offered the opportunity to pay restitution to the consumer in instead of the fines and/or penalties, or to have the penalty reduced.

### Hearing process

You are entitled to hire an attorney and to bring that attorney to the hearing. The DMV is the petitioner is this case and the complainant may be a witness for the case.

As a result of the hearing, the ALJ may sustain some, all, or none of the charges. There may be no action, a warning, the imposition of a suspension, revocation, and/or civil penalties. If the ALJ only imposes civil penalties, in order to prevent the loss of your operating privilege, you must pay all fines and penalties. You will receive a letter from the DMV shortly after the hearing. You will have 30 days from the date of the order by the judge to pay your fine or penalty.

Failure to pay any fines or penalties or to serve out your suspension will result in indefinite suspension of your business certificate and the possible assessment of a lien against your business. However, if you pay your fine and/or penalty or serve out your period of suspension, you will be back in business after complete compliance. If you are revoked, you must surrender all supplies and cease to operate.

You have the right to appeal any adverse decision. If you chose to appeal, you have 60 days from the date of the ALJs decision to file the Appeal From DMV Hearing Determination (pdf) [2] (AA-33A), which must be accompanied by the appropriate filing fee.

Your facility license, registration or certification enables you to operate in New York State. Complaints filed and charges brought against you can result in the loss of your privilege to operate as a business here.

# 关于对检测站和认证检查员的投诉与收费

如果您想对检测站或认证检查员提出投诉，请举报与DMV监管的汽车业务相关的问题 [1]。

### 针对您或您的企业提出的投诉

纽约州机动车管理局（DMV）监管纽约州所有修理厂、检测站、经销商、车辆拆解商及其他相关企业。要合法经营此类业务，您必须在DMV注册。申请获批后，您将收到DMV颁发的证书，同时也会收到一份与您业务类型相关的《专员条例》副本，其中会说明您对消费者的责任。您必须遵守所有消费者保护法律和法规。

DMV建议所有对经销商、检测站、修理厂或拆解商有投诉的消费者，先尝试与业务经理解决问题。若未能解决，建议联系DMV消费者与设施服务投诉部门。

- 保护您的业务：将所有工单副本存放在易于取用的位置

### 投诉流程

如果针对您的投诉已提交，DMV的消费者服务代表（CSR）将与您联系以尝试解决该投诉。CSR会说明投诉性质，并告知您的权利、责任及应承担的法律责任。若投诉未能通过CSR解决，案件将转交给汽车设施检查员（AFI）进行正式调查。

- 及时回应所有DMV问询，以避免昂贵的罚款、处罚及失去宝贵客户

### 调查流程

AFI将进行正式调查。结果可能是不采取行动、将警告信（调查通知）存入您的档案，或由行政法法官（ALJ）主持正式行政听证。当车辆安全部门启动听证程序时，您可能会收到通过“听证弃权书”承认指控并支付特定罚款和/或接受停业处罚的机会。若接受弃权，则无需听证；若拒绝，则必须举行听证。

听证结果可能是不采取行动、民事罚款，和/或暂停或撤销您在纽约州经营车辆相关业务的资格。您也可能有机会向消费者支付赔偿金以代替罚款和/或处罚，或获得减轻处罚。

### 听证流程

您有权聘请律师并带其出席听证。在此案中，DMV是申诉方，投诉人可能作为证人出庭。

听证结束后，ALJ可能维持部分、全部或全部不维持指控。结果可能是不采取行动、警告、暂停、撤销和/或民事罚款。若ALJ仅处以民事罚款，为防止失去经营资格，您必须支付所有罚款和处罚。听证后不久，您将收到DMV的信函，需在法官裁决之日起30天内支付罚款或处罚。

未能支付任何罚款或处罚或未执行停业处罚，将导致您的营业执照无限期暂停，并可能对您的企业进行留置权评估。但是，若您支付罚款和/或处罚或完成停业期，完全合规后即可恢复营业。若被撤销资格，您必须交出所有用品并停止运营。

您有权对任何不利决定提出上诉。若选择上诉，需在ALJ裁决之日起60天内提交《DMV听证决定上诉书》（PDF）[2]（AA-33A），并附上相应的申请费。

您的设施许可证、注册或认证使您能够在纽约州运营。针对您提出的投诉和指控可能导致您失去在此经营业务的资格。

如果标签无法使用，您可以重新检查车辆，或使用《更换检查标签申请表》（PDF）[8]（VS-118）订购替换标签。填写表格并邮寄至表格上的地址。

chunk_id: About New York State Inspections#3_0::c0023

heading_path: 关于纽约州车辆检查
我需要更换检查标签
text:
[关于纽约州车辆检查 > 我需要更换检查标签]
您可以重新检查车辆，或使用《更换检查标签申请表》（PDF）[8]（VS-118）订购替换标签。填写表格并邮寄至表格上的地址。

检查站会将所有排放检查记录以电子方式发送给DMV。DMV必须有一份记录，证明您的车辆在过去一年内通过了排放检查。请保留排放检查标签的收据，以证明您的车辆已接受检查。 如果您车辆上的检查标签在过去60天内过期，您可能会被处以25至50美元的罚款。如果检查标签过期超过60天，罚款在50至100美元之间。如果没有检查标签，罚款在50至100美元之间。此外，还需支付88美元（城镇和乡村法院为93美元）的强制性州附加费。 停放车辆如果没有检查标签或检查标签过期，可能会收到停车罚单。 以下车辆免于排放检查： - 摩托车 - 车龄少于两个车型年（车型年大于或等于日历年减一） - 车龄超过25个车型年（车型年小于或等于日历年减25） - 柴油动力车辆，但1997年及以后且总车重额定值（GVRW）低于8,501磅的柴油动力车辆除外 - 电动车辆 - 发放历史牌照的车辆 - 需接受重型车辆安全检查的车辆

heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
什么是I-PIRP/ADM项目？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 什么是I-PIRP/ADM项目？]
I-PIRP/ADM是互联网积分与保险减免项目/替代授课方式的缩写。该项目允许经批准的赞助商通过互联网或其他替代授课方式（如DVD或数字有线电视）提供防御性驾驶/事故预防课程。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0001
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
谁提供I-PIRP课程？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 谁提供I-PIRP课程？]
您必须确保在纽约州参加的任何用于积分和保险减免的课程都是纽约州DMV批准的课程。请参阅DMV批准的I-PIRP课程赞助商列表[1]。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0002
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
如果我参加I-PIRP课程，我能获得积分和保险减免吗？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 如果我参加I-PIRP课程，我能获得积分和保险减免吗？]
是的。当您完成I-PIRP课程后，您将获得与完成课堂PIRP课程相同的福利。您的驾驶违规积分总数最多可减少四分，并且您可以在汽车责任险和碰撞险保费上节省百分之十。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0003
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
完成I-PIRP课程需要多长时间？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 完成I-PIRP课程需要多长时间？]
I-PIRP课程要求至少320分钟的教学时间。教学时间不包括注册、验证您的身份和参与情况，或下载和参加任何测试所需的时间。课程网站设有控制措施，以确保您满足所有要求，并且您至少有320分钟的教学时间。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0004
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
I-PIRP课程与课堂课程相比如何？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > I-PIRP课程与课堂课程相比如何？]
课堂PIRP课程和I-PIRP课程的内容和信息非常相似，两门课程都包含320分钟的教学。课堂课程在一个白天的时段或两个晚上的时段进行。您可以在方便的时间在家参加I-PIRP课程。您必须在注册课程之日起30天内完成I-PIRP课程。您可以在30天期限内按照自己的进度参加I-PIRP课程。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0005
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
我可以退出并在稍后继续I-PIRP课程，或者在不同的计算机上分别进行课程会话吗？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 我可以退出并在稍后继续I-PIRP课程，或者在不同的计算机上分别进行课程会话吗？]
是的。您可以根据需要分多次完成课程，但必须在注册后30个日历日内完成课程。

您的数据将在线存储，用于每个课程会话。大多数赞助商在您注册课程时会为您分配一个用户ID和密码。您可以使用您的ID和密码在任何能够以可接受的连接访问互联网的计算机上登录。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0006
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
I-PIRP课程有测验或期末考试吗？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > I-PIRP课程有测验或期末考试吗？]
I-PIRP课程可以有在线测验、随机测试和/或期末考试，以验证您的参与情况并确定您是否理解课程内容。一些赞助商可能要求您亲自参加期末考试。测试要求将在您注册课程之前说明，通常在课程的条款与条件部分。

除了关于课程内容的知识测试外，还会有问题来帮助验证您的身份和课程参与情况。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0007
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
如果我测验、测试或期末考试不及格怎么办？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 如果我测验、测试或期末考试不及格怎么办？]
测试和考试流程及成绩的影响因主办方而异。在注册课程之前，请仔细阅读有关测试的信息。

该课程通常要求您正确回答70%的课程内容问题。通常，您有两次机会来获得问题的正确答案。

测试有时间限制，在测试期间您查找未知答案的时间有限。建议您在开始测试之前复习章节内容。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0008
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
如果我未通过课程怎么办？我可以获得课程费用退款吗？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 如果我未通过课程怎么办？我可以获得课程费用退款吗？]
如果您未满足完成课程的所有要求或未达到最低测试分数要求，您将无法获得课程完成学分，也无法获得该课程的积分和保险减免。

主办方可以免费为您提供再次参加同一课程的机会。主办方并非必须提供此服务。

doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
I-PIRP课程的费用是多少？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > I-PIRP课程的费用是多少？]
费用由课程主办方设定，不同课程的费用各不相同。在注册课程之前，您的费用已明确说明。比较课程及其费用对您有利。

text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 我如何支付I-PIRP课程费用？]
主办方通常要求您使用信用卡支付，但这由各主办方决定。请与主办方联系以获取有关支付的完整信息。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0011

heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
课程取消和/或退款的程序是什么？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 课程取消和/或退款的程序是什么？]
如果主办方无法进行课程或课程的任何部分，他们必须为您提供全额退还所有课程费用的选项。主办方还可以在课程可用时为您提供重新安排课程的选项。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0012
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
参加I-PIRP课程需要什么类型的设备和科技？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 参加I-PIRP课程需要什么类型的设备和科技？]
答案取决于课程的替代授课方式（ADM）。例如，如果课程是网络课程，您必须有一台计算机和可接受的互联网连接。对于DVD ADM课程，您必须有电视和DVD播放器。主办方必须提供授课所需的任何额外技术。主办方必须在您注册课程时告知您这些要求。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0013
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
我如何以及何时收到课程完成证书？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 我如何以及何时收到课程完成证书？]
课程主办方通过普通邮件将课程完成证书邮寄给您。证书的电子邮件副本无效，您的保险公司不会接受。

课程主办方必须在课程完成后的14个工作日内颁发课程完成证书。一些主办方提供额外收费的快递邮寄选项。

heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
DMV是否会将我的完成证书直接发送给我的汽车保险公司？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > DMV是否会将我的完成证书直接发送给我的汽车保险公司？]
不。您必须联系保险公司并向他们提供您的证书，以获得保险减免优惠。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0015
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
I-PIRP网站是否安全？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > I-PIRP网站是否安全？]
是的。DMV要求主办方及其交付代理提供安全的网站，以保护参加课程者的个人信息。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0016
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
参加课程需要提供哪些个人信息？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 参加课程需要提供哪些个人信息？]
主办方收集个人信息以验证您的身份和参与情况。这可能包括身份信息，如您纽约州驾照上的DMV ID号（客户ID号）、您的姓名和出生日期。您应确保使用与纽约州驾照上完全一致的姓名（不要使用昵称）。主办方还将收集信用卡信息以支付课程费用。

身份和参与信息还可能包括生物识别信息，如击键、面部识别或语音识别。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0017
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
完成课程后，我的个人信息会被保留吗？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 完成课程后，我的个人信息会被保留吗？]
请阅读I-PIRP主办方网站上的隐私和安全信息。主办方被要求在DMV规定的时间段内将您的个人信息存储在安全的服务器上。

DMV会验证托管课程的服务器安全性。

chunk_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0::c0018
doc_id: About online and alternative delivery method courses (I-PIRP/ADM)#3_0
heading_path: 关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM）
如何确保注册课程的人就是参加课程的人？
text:
[关于在线和替代授课方式课程（I-PIRP/ADM） > 如何确保注册课程的人就是参加课程的人？]
每个课程主办方都有不同的方法来验证注册课程的人与参加课程的人是同一人。任何试图欺骗系统或接受课程完成证书及其相关优惠而未亲自完成整个课程的人，均构成犯罪，可能面临起诉、罚款和监禁。

重要提示：如果您没有纽约州DMV ID号（客户ID号），则ADM课程完成情况无法应用到您的驾照记录中。在尝试参加ADM课程之前，您可能需要提交《驾驶员和/或车辆记录信息申请表》（PDF）[2]（MV-15）。

text:
# About point reduction

## Completing a Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP) course does not remove a violation,

conviction, or the number of points from your driving record. Even after you complete the course, most violations, convictions and points will continue to show on your driving record for up to 4 years. Violations and convictions involving drugs or alcohol will remain on your driving record for ten or fifteen years, depending on the violation. If you get 11 points for traffic violations in an 18-month period, your driver license may be suspended. "Point reduction" means the number of points on your driving record used to calculate the number of total points received within 18 months will be reduced by 4 points and may help you avoid a suspension. See About the NY State Point System [1] for more information about how points are calculated.

## How do | receive the point reduction?

The PIRP course sponsor will notify the DMV within 10 weeks after you complete the course. DMV will then reduce the active points on your driving record by up to 4 points.

## How do | know my driving record shows my PIRP course completion?

If you need to verify that your course completion is on your DMV record, you can request a copy of your driving record [2].

If your course completion is not recorded on your driving record more than 10 weeks after you completed it, contact the course sponsor.

## What effect does point reduction have on my license and driving record?

- Point reduction applies only to points assessed for violations that occurred within the eighteen months immediately before course completion. It does not affect points for earlier violations, and cannot be used as "credit" against future violations or points.

- Point reduction cannot reduce your point total lower than zero.

- If your license has already been revoked or suspended, the point reduction will not affect that action.

- If a violation hearing has already been scheduled, the point reduction will not affect that action.

- Point reduction does not prevent or cancel a mandatory revocation or suspension for violations such as DWI, DWAI, or three speeding violations within 18 months.

- You can only use a Point & Insurance Reduction Program course to reduce points once in a 18-month period.

- The DMV point system and your insurance company s "point" systems are separate and not related. Point reduction on your driving record does not affect points assigned by your insurance company for violations and accidents. Completion of a course under the Point & Insurance Reduction Program also cannot prevent or reduce the calculation of points affecting a Driver Responsibility Assessment. [3]

# Learn how to reduce your insurance rate. [4]

# About Private Service Bureau Licenses

# About Private Service Bureau Licenses [1]

A Private Service Bureau (PSB) license is required of any person, firm, association or corporation engaged in the business of assisting for hire in securing licenses to drive motor vehicles, registrations, or titles of motor vehicles.

### How to Apply

#### Request Name Approval

Before you can apply for a license to operate a PSB, you must first submit a Name Selection Form for PSB Applicants [2] (PSB-3) and receive approval from the DMV. To avoid public confusion, a name that includes "DMV" or "Motor Vehicles" will not be approved.

#### Application Requirements

To apply for a license to operate a PSB, you must submit to the NY State DMV

- your form PSB-3 that shows your PSB name was approved by the DMV (see above)
- a photocopy of a valid NY State driver license or non-driver photo ID card for the business owner(s) and all employees of the PSB
- a completed Application for a License to Operate a Private Service Bureau or Open a Branch Office [3] (MV-372)
- a completed Personal History [4] (MV-521.1) for each owner, partner, corporate officer, agent, employee and major stockholder (20% or more of stock) listed on Form MV-372
- a copy of the receipt provided to clients as required by Section 77.5 of the Regulations of the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles. See Sample Receipt Form [5] (PSB-2).
- if you do not have employees, you must submit a completed Form CE-200 (Certificate of Attestation of Exemption from NY State Workers Compensation) available from the NY State Worker's Compensation Board [6]. This form is to show a government agency that NY State Workers Compensation insurance is not required.
- if you have employees, you must submit your proof of current Workers Compensation and Disability Insurance Coverage
- a Business Certificate (X-201), a Business Certificate for Partnerships (X-74) or NY State Department of State Filing Receipt (DOS-1025)
- the application fee of $25.00 (non-refundable). Make checks payable to Commissioner of Motor Vehicles.

Send all required items to:

NYS Department of Motor VehiclesPartnering Programs, Room 3226 Empire State PlazaAlbany, NY 12228

### What to expect after you apply

After your application is reviewed by the DMV in Albany, it is sent to your local Motor Vehicle office. The local office schedules an inspection. When the inspector visits your location, the inspector can ask you to provide the following for review

- the original lease
- the original business certificate and/or corporate papers and/or filing receipt
- a sample customer receipt
- a permanent, bound book
- a filing cabinet
- your proof of Workers Compensation Insurance (if required)
- three character reference letters.

### Renew your PSB License

A PSB license expires every two years on June 30. Use Application for Private Service Bureau License Renewal [7] (MV372R) to apply to renew your PSB license.

If you have any questions, call 1-518-473-6586.

[关于问题驾驶员限制 > 问题驾驶员限制可以应用于哪些驾照类别？]
如果你有问题驾驶员限制，你只能驾驶

- 往返于你的工作地点
- 在你的工作时间内，如果你的职业要求操作机动车
- 往返于必要的医疗预约，该预约是你或你家庭成员的必要医疗治疗的一部分（你可能需要提供来自你的持牌医疗提供者的书面声明，以证明该出行是必要的）
- 往返于机动车管理局办公室，以办理与包含问题驾驶员限制的驾照/许可证/特权相关的业务
- 往返于孩子的学校/日托中心，如果孩子在该学校/日托中心出勤对于你维持就业或维持在被认可的学校、学院或大学或州批准的职业技术培训机构注册是必要的
- 往返于你注册的被认可的学校、学院或大学或州批准的职业技术培训机构

这些限制在DMV发给你的附件中列出。你在操作机动车时必须携带该附件。

问题驾驶员限制只能应用于D类驾照。它不能应用于任何商业驾驶执照（CDL）A、B或C类，初级驾驶员执照DJ类，摩托车驾驶员执照M或MJ类，或E类驾驶员执照。

text:
[关于问题驾驶员限制 > 如果我在获得带有问题驾驶员限制的驾驶员执照或许可证之前有移动违规定罪，会发生什么？]
如果您因以下任何违规行为被定罪，带有问题驾驶员限制的驾驶执照或许可证将被撤销

- 跟车过近（追尾）
- 超速、竞速
- 超出限制驾驶
- 使用手机或发短信违规
- 鲁莽驾驶
- 任何其他两项交通违规。这包括车辆操作员未系安全带，但不包括停车、停靠、站立、设备、检查或其他非移动违规。

您的驾驶执照将被吊销至少30天。之后您可以向DIU申请新驾照，并必须支付不可退还的$100申请费。

# 关于纽约州驾驶员记分制度

### 什么是驾驶员违规记分制度，它是如何运作的？

驾驶员违规记分制度使纽约州车管所能够识别并对高风险驾驶员采取行动。车管所会对某些交通违规行为进行记分。如果在18个月内累计达到11分，您的驾驶执照可能会被吊销。1 然而，记分制度并不是失去驾照的唯一途径（见吊销和撤销[1]）。

### 如何计算您的总分

- 您必须因交通违规被定罪后，分数才会被添加到您的驾驶记录中
- 您的总分是根据违规日期计算的，而不是定罪日期
- 将过去18个月内发生的所有违规行为的分数相加，即可计算出您的总分2

### 常见交通违规行为的记分数

### 以下违规行为不记分

- 任何自行车违规
- 任何行人违规
- 任何停车违规
- 任何与未注册、未取得驾照或未投保驾驶相关的违规
- 任何与机动车检验、车辆重量或尺寸或车辆设备（除制动器不足外）相关的违规
- 任何与《车辆与交通法》或任何地方法律中规定的商业或商品销售相关的违规
- 在萨福克县长岛高速公路49号出口至57号出口之间不当使用高占用率车辆车道相关的违规
- 任何其他非因驾驶机动车而导致的违规

### 驾驶员责任评估

如果您在18个月内在纽约州驾驶记录上累计达到6分或以上，您必须支付驾驶员责任评估费[2]。

### 州外定罪

如果您在另一个州或国家因交通违规被定罪，除非违规发生在安大略省或魁北克省，否则分数不会添加到您的纽约州驾驶记录中。

纽约州与魁北克省和安大略省签订了互惠协议。在这些省份发生的交通违规定罪将记录在您的纽约州驾驶记录中，并且这些定罪与在纽约州发生的定罪具有相同的效力并携带相同的分数。这可能会影响您的驾驶员违规总分和驾驶员责任评估。

### 保险费

保险公司有自己的记分制度，并可能根据您的驾驶记录提高您的保费。请联系您的保险公司以获取更多信息。

### 记分与保险减免计划

参加经车管所批准的记分与保险减免计划（PIRP）课程将

- 帮助防止您在驾驶记录上累计达到11分或以上时失去驾照
  - 如果您有11分或以上，为暂停驾照之目的，将“减去”4分
  - 罚单/分数会从您的驾驶记录中实际移除
- 在您的汽车责任险和碰撞险保费上节省10%

进一步了解PIRP课程[3]。

### 查询我的积分

您可以使用MyDMV的“我的驾照、许可证或身份证”服务来查询您的积分。您需要提供纽约州颁发的以下证件上的身份证号和证件号：

- 驾驶执照，
- 学习许可证，或
- 非驾驶员身份证

如果您丢失了证件，最近续办或订购了新证件但尚未通过邮件收到，您需要等待其到达后才能创建MyDMV账户。

通过MyDMV查询我的积分[4] [4]

- 1. 如果您声称他人对您记录上的违规行为负责，您可以请求听证会。但您不能请求DMV听证会来证明您对违规行为无罪。
- 2. 一旦自违规日期起已过去18个月，该违规行为的积分不再计入您的总分。然而，只要定罪记录仍在您的记录上，这些积分就会保留在您的驾驶记录中，并可能被您的保险公司用于提高保费。

# 添加和移除用户

当DMV创建LENS名册时，我们会向申请人发放个人用户ID和密码。如果您的组织中有多人可能使用LENS，我们很乐意为您发放额外的用户ID。每位LENS用户都可以且应该拥有自己的个人登录凭据。请勿与他人共享您的登录信息或密码。

### 如何添加用户？

要获取额外的用户ID，请发送电子邮件至[email protected] [2]，并提供以下所有信息

- 您的5位数LENS名册编号
- 用户的纽约州驾驶执照/非驾驶员ID号码1
- 用户的完整姓名
- 企业名称
- 用户的办公地址
- 用户的办公电话号码
- 用户的办公电子邮件地址

然后我们将

- 将用户ID发送至用户的办公电子邮件地址，以及
- 将密码邮寄至用户的个人执照/ID邮寄地址。

密码是我们唯一发送到用户个人邮寄地址的LENS信息。我们不会将密码发送到办公地址。

### 如何移除用户？

如果LENS用户离开您的组织，您可以通过完成以下步骤将其移除：

1. 登录LENS
2. 访问LENS主菜单并选择“客户信息”
3. 选择“用户配置文件维护”
4. 点击“搜索”以列出您的所有LENS用户
5. 找到离职用户并勾选相应的“移除”框。点击“处理”。

如果LENS用户离开您的组织且您无法登录LENS，请发送电子邮件至[email protected] [2]。请注明该用户和您的LENS客户编号。我们将禁用已离职用户对您的LENS名册的访问权限。

### 如何更改用户？

如果有人接替另一用户的职责，请按照上述主题中的说明请求额外的用户ID。请勿与前用户共享前用户的ID和密码。我们不会为任何使用他人用户ID的人提供支持。一旦发现共享用户ID，我们可能会撤销这些ID。

To report a change of address for your business, you must complete a Statement of Ownership and/or Permission to Use Place of Business (pdf) [2] (VS-19).

You can also call the DMV Office of Vehicle Safety and Clean Air at 1-518-474-4653 to get the form, or call 1-518-474-0919 to get more information.

# Appeal a TVB ticket conviction

# Appeal a TVB ticket conviction [1]

### You can appeal a Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB) conviction online or by mail

- you must file your appeal within 30 days of the date of conviction
- you must pay a $10 non refundable appeal fee for each conviction appealed within 30 days of the date of conviction 1

Your submission of an appeal online or by mail does not mean that your appeal has been accepted. The DMV Appeals Board must determine that your appeal meets legal requirements. 2

### Online

#### You can appeal online if

- you have been convicted in a NYS Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB) for a traffic offense
- the conviction occurred within the last 30 days 3

The traffic ticket must display the words "Traffic Violations Bureau" at the bottom. If it does not, you cannot file an appeal with the Department of Motor Vehicles. 4

At the end of the transaction you will get a 3-digit Appeal Access number. You can use this later to check the status of your appeal.

You can appeal one transaction (conviction) online at a time.

#### You will need

- the TVB traffic ticket number from your conviction (see a sample ticket [2])

and either

- your DMV ID Number (Client ID Number) from your NYS driver license, learner permit or non-driver photo ID card (see a sample driver license [3])

or

- you full name, date of birth, and gender (as they appear on the traffic ticket)

and the following

- your mailing address (please note that any address you enter for the appeal will not automatically update your DMV driver license or vehicle records)
- an Appeal Argument that explains the valid reasons for your appeal
- if an attorney will represent you in the appeal, the attorney's name and mailing address
- if you request a stay of a suspension or revocation that resulted from the conviction, a written 'Stay Argument'

You must notify the DMV Appeals Board in writing immediately of any change of address that occurs after an appeal is filed.

Appeal a TVB ticket conviction online [4]

#### Exhibits or arguments that can't be submitted online

You can mail DMV any exhibits or arguments that cannot be submitted online. Evidence, exhibits or documents not submitted to and considered by the hearing officer may not be filed with the appeal. 6

#### You cannot cancel an online appeal

You cannot cancel your transaction after you verify your information or submit your payment.

#### You cannot edit your online appeal

You cannot edit your original Appeal Argument or any Additional Appeal Arguments after you submit online.

#### You can submit an additional Appeal Argument

If you request a transcript to be reviewed for your online appeal, you may submit an additional Appeal Argument. The Additional Argument must be submitted within 30 days after the transcript you ordered has been sent to you from the Transcriber. To submit an Additional Argument after receiving your transcript, access the transaction again and enter either

- the ticket number
- your DMV ID Number (Client ID Number) from your NYS driver license, learner permit or non-driver photo ID card (see sample driver license [3])

or, your

- name
- date of birth
- (3-digit) Appeal Access Number

### By mail

Use the Traffic Violations Bureau Appeal [5] (AA-33) form. Mail your appeal and $10 appeal fee to

DMV Appeals BoardP.O. Box 2935Albany, NY 12220-0935

To appeal a DMV determination other than a TVB conviction or penalty, use the Appeal From DMV Hearing Determination [6] (AA-33A).

### By phone

Sorry, you cannot appeal a TVB conviction by phone.

### At a TVB office

Sorry, you cannot submit an appeal at a TVB office.

### How to check the status of appeal filed online

The Appeals Board will acknowledge receipt of your appeal form and fee with a letter.

You can also use the TVB Traffic Ticket Appeal service to check your appeal status. You will need to provide

- the ticket number
- your DMV ID Number (Client ID Number) from your NYS driver license, learner permit or non-driver photo ID card

or, your

- name
- date of birth
- (3-digit) Appeal Access Number

 

- 1. Your appeal is not refundable. Whether your appeal is rejected, or the conviction or penalty is affirmed, reversed, remanded, or modified, the appeal fee cannot be refunded.

- 2. The DMV Appeals Board will reject your appeal if
  - your appeal form and fee are not filed in a timely manner
  - your appeal does not meet the requirements of NYS law
  - the matter is not legally allowed to be appealed
  - you fail to meet DMV requirements for appeals

- 3. For default convictions, you can appeal the denial of your application to reopen the default conviction only after the DMV TVB Default Unit has denied your Application to Reopen a Default Conviction [7] (AA-3.3)

- 4. The TVB does not process, and you cannot file an appeal with the DMV for any conviction or penalty that

- occurred in a local court
  - resulted from a parking ticket
  - resulted from a criminal violation

You must appeal these kinds of penalties and convictions with the local court or parking violations authority, not the Department of Motor Vehicles.

- 5. The Stay Argument must explain the reasons why you need a stay. Filing an appeal does not change your obligation to pay the fine, surcharge, or other fees. The DMV will not grant a stay of a suspension for failure to pay a fine, surcharge or suspension termination fee.

- 6. To submit exhibits or arguments that cannot be submitted through the online transaction.

- If you submit the additional exhibits and/or arguments at the time you file the appeal online, check the box in the transaction that indicates that you will mail additional exhibits and/or arguments for your appeal.
  - If you order a transcript for your appeal, you must mail the additional arguments to the Appeals Board within 30 days after the transcript you ordered has been sent to you.
  - If you do not want or need a transcript, you must mail the exhibits and/or arguments within 10 days of the day you submit your appeal.
  - Evidence, exhibits or documents not submitted to and considered by the hearing officer may not be filed with the appeal.
  - The Appeals Board uses the US Postal Service postmark, if legible, to determine if your documents are timely. Keep your proof of mailing and a copy of anything you send to the Appeals Board.
  - Write the summons number of the appealed ticket on the front of the envelope and on all exhibits and/or arguments.

Mail your documents to

DMV Appeals BoardP.O. Box 2935Albany, NY 12220-0935

## Do it by mail:

If you do not wantto file an appeal online, use Traffic Violations Bureau Appeal (AA-33).

To appeal a DMV determination other than a TVB conviction or penalty, use form Appeal Form (AA-33A). Mail your appeal and fee(s) to

DMV Appeals BoardP.O. Box 2935Albany, NY 12220-0935

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0000
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
ATV REGISTRATION AND DATE OF EXPIRATION
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > ATV REGISTRATION AND DATE OF EXPIRATION]
An all-terrain vehicle (ATV) is any self-propelled vehicle with two or more wheels that is manufactured for sale to be used primarily off-highway or in off-road competitions, and that is no wider than 70 inches and weighs no more than 1,000 pounds. This does not include vehicles manufactured for off-highway use and designed exclusively for travel on snow or ice, and supported by one or more skis, belts or cleats that utilize an endless belt tread. Those vehicles, which include snowmobiles, are subject to other laws and regulations.

An ATV must be registered with the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) if it is operated anywhere in New York State, including on the owner's property.

When you register a new or used ATV for the first time, your registration will expire each year on August 31. Registrations for ATVs originally registered before April 1, 2005, will continue to expire each year on April 30.

ATV dealers are required by law to register every ATV they sell to New York State residents or to non-residents before the purchaser takes delivery; unless the purchaser qualifies for an exemption from registration. A purchaser is exempt from registration when the ATV will be used exclusively: outside of New York State; at special events; for agricultural purposes; or for snow plowing other than for-hire. Dealers must have the purchaser complete and sign a "Declaration of Exemption From Snowmobile or All-Terrain Vehicle Registration" (RV-6).

Unless you qualify for an exemption from registration, you cannot take delivery from an authorized dealer until after the ATV is registered.

If you buy an ATV from a person who is not a New York State registered ATV dealer, you must register the ATV with the DMV. To register the ATV; you must complete an "Vehicle Registration/Title Application [1]" (MV-82) and submit it to a motor vehicle issuing office. To register an ATV; you must provide proofs of ownership, sales tax payment or exemption, your identity, and your date of birth.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0001
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
PROOF OF OWNERSHIP
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > PROOF OF OWNERSHIP]
Acceptable proof of ownership are:

- For a new ATV the manufacturer's certificate or statement of origin (MCO or MSO), an out-of-state title certificate or registration certificate; or,
- For a used ATV a completed "Certification of Sale or Transfer [2]" (MV-51) plus the MCO or MSO; or, a New York State transferable registration signed over to you by the previous owner.
- If your ATV has never been registered and you do not have these acceptable documents, you must complete and submit a "Statement of Ownership [3]" (MV-51B).

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0002
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
PROOF OF SALES TAX PAYMENT
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > PROOF OF SALES TAX PAYMENT]
If you buy your ATV from a registered New York State dealer, you should receive a bill of sale in addition to the acceptable documents that prove ownership. The bill of sale must contain the dealer's name, address and dealer registration number, plus your name and address, the ATV vehicle identification number, the year, make, model, and number of wheels. The bill of sale also must indicate that the ATV is either new or used, and must confirm that the dealer has collected the appropriate sales tax.

If you buy the ATV from a person who is not a registered dealer, you must pay the sales tax at a motor vehicle office. To determine the proper amount of sales tax, the DMV needs proof of what you paid for the ATV. Have the seller sign and give you a Statement of Transaction- Sale or Gift of Motor Vehicle, Trailer, All-Terrain Vehicle (ATV), Vessel (Boat), or Snowmobile (pdf) [4] (at NY State Department of Tax and Finance) (DTF-802). You must submit this form to the motor vehicle office, and pay the appropriate sales tax, before registering your ATV:

Acceptable documents that prove payment of sales tax are:

- The dealer's bill of sale showing that the dealer had collected the sales tax; or
- A receipt for sales tax payment from the motor vehicle office.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0003
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
PROOF OF IDENTITY AND DATE OF BIRTH
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > PROOF OF IDENTITY AND DATE OF BIRTH]
To register an ATV, you must provide proof of who you are. You must provide proof of identity, date of birth, and at least six points of proof of name. For the most recent listing of acceptable documents see "Proofs of Identity For Registration and Title [5]" (ID-82).

Documents that automatically qualify as six points are:

- NY State Photo Driver license or Learner Permit
- NY State Non-Driver Photo Identification Card

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0004
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
FEES
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > FEES]
The ATV registration and registration renewal fee is $12.50 per year it is not prorated by month. You also must pay a $12.50 license plate fee when you first register your ATV. You will be issued a plate, a registration sticker and an attached registration document. The plate must be attached to the rear of the ATV, and the sticker should be placed at the right side of the plate. You should carry the registration document when operating your ATV.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0005
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
INSURANCE
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > INSURANCE]
You may not operate any ATV anywhere in New York State, except on your own property, unless it is covered by liability insurance. Minimum required coverage is $50,000/$100,000 for death, $25,000/$50,000 for injury, and $10,000 for property damage in any one accident. You must show proof of this insurance upon the request of a judge, the police, or a person claiming to have suffered injury or property damage from your operation of the ATV.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0006
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
CHANGE OF ADDRESS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > CHANGE OF ADDRESS]
If you move, cross out the old address on your registration document and write in the new one. You also must report your address change to the DMV [6] within 10 days.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0007
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
THEFT, DESTRUCTION, REMOVAL FROM THE STATE
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > THEFT, DESTRUCTION, REMOVAL FROM THE STATE]
If your ATV has become stolen, you should immediately report the theft to the police. If the ATV is to be, or already has been, destroyed or permanently removed from New York State, you should surrender the plate and registration document to a local motor vehicle office.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0008
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
OUT-OF-STATE REGISTRATIONS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > OUT-OF-STATE REGISTRATIONS]
New York State honors valid out-of-state ATV registrations. If your home state does not require ATV registration, you must obtain a New York State registration before operating your ATV in this state.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0009
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
WHO MAY OPERATE AN ATV
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > WHO MAY OPERATE AN ATV]
You do not need a driver license to operate an ATV in New York State, but certain restrictions apply to operators under age 16.

If you are age 10 through age 15, you may operate an ATV only:

- Under adult supervision; or,
- Without adult supervision on lands owned or leased by your parent or guardian; or,
- On any lands where ATV use is permitted, without adult supervision, if you have completed an ATV safety training course approved by the DMV. You should carry your course completion certificate when operating any ATV.

If you are under age 10, you may operate an ATV only:

- Under adult supervision; or,
- Without adult supervision on lands owned or leased by your parent or guardian.

Adult Supervision means being accompanied by a person at least 18 years of age, or a person 16 or 17 years of age who holds an ATV safety course completion certificate from an approved safety course provider.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0010
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
SAFETY TRAINING AND INFORMATION
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > SAFETY TRAINING AND INFORMATION]
ATV safety training courses approved by the Department of Motor Vehicles are available throughout the state. Telephone 1-800-887-2887 to enroll, or write to: ATV Safety Institute, Enrollment Express, 2 Jenner Street, Suite 150, Irvine, CA 92618-3806

ATV safety information also is available on the internet at www.nyatvsafety.net [7]. Written questions about New York State's ATV or motorcycle safety programs should be addressed through the DMV web site or by mail:

NYS DMV Motorcycle Safety Program6 Empire State Plaza, Room 335Albany, New York 12228

The application forms identified in this publication for ATV owners and operators are available at any motor vehicle office or at the DMV web site: dmv.ny.gov [8]

RESPONSIBILITY OF PARENTS AND OWNERS

A parent or guardian may not knowingly permit or authorize his or her child under age 16 to operate an ATV in violation of state or local laws. An ATV owner, or another person in possession of an ATV, may not knowingly permit or authorize any person under age 16 to operate an ATV in violation of any state or local law.

Both the owner and the operator of an ATV may be held liable for injury and/or damages resulting from an ATV accident.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0011
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
WHERE AND WHEN TO DRIVE ACROSS HIGHWAYS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > WHERE AND WHEN TO DRIVE ACROSS HIGHWAYS]
DMV recommends you avoid crossing a highway unless absolutely necessary. If you cross, you must follow these rules:

- You must cross at an angle of approximately 90 degrees, at a place where there are no obstructions to prevent a quick, safe crossing.
- You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic on the highway before crossing.
- You may cross a divided highway only where it intersects with another street or highway.
- You may not cross an interstate highway or any controlled-access highway, such as the Thruway or a parkway at any time.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0012
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
ON HIGHWAYS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > ON HIGHWAYS]
You may not operate an ATV on a highway unless it has been designated and posted for ATV use by the state or local authority. Usually, only the part of a highway between two off-highway trails will be posted for ATV use. Check with local police to be sure. DMV recommends that you turn your headlight and taillight on and wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride on a highway. Always enter the highway with care, and yield to other traffic.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0013
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
ON PUBLIC LAND
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > ON PUBLIC LAND]
You may not operate an ATV on public land unless it is specifically designated for ATV use, and it is allowed by a posted sign.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0014
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
ON PRIVATE LAND
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > ON PRIVATE LAND]
To operate an ATV on private land, you must have permission of the land owner or lessee. If you receive permission, make sure you know the boundaries of the property, and respect any special restrictions or requests of the land owner. You could lose permission to ride on private land by littering, causing damage, or riding carelessly.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0015
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
REQUIRED EQUIPMENT
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > REQUIRED EQUIPMENT]
Whether you are the operator or passenger, you must wear a USDOT-approved helmet when riding an ATV. DMV recommends that you also wear a face shield or goggles, and protective clothes and footwear.

Your ATV must have the following equipment:

- Brakes in good condition
- A muffler which is in good operating condition and meets federal standards
- A spark arrester approved by the U.S. Forest Service
- Tires with at least 2/32nds of an inch tread without visible breaks, cuts, exposed cords, bumps or bulges
- A lighted white headlight and red taillight if the ATV is driven at night

The law requires you to keep the ATV's headlight and taillight lighted when riding a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise. For greater safety, DMV recommends you keep the lights on at all times.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0016
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
RIDING RESTRICTIONS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > RIDING RESTRICTIONS]
In addition to obeying the ATV laws and rules, it is wise to ride your ATV with common sense and courtesy. Having fun on an ATV does not include annoying others or taking foolish risks. ATV riders who ignore the rules and the rights of others may cause ATV operation to be restricted or prohibited on private and public lands.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0017
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
YOU MAY NEVER OPERATE AN ATV
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > YOU MAY NEVER OPERATE AN ATV]
- Other than while seated on the permanent, regular seat.
- With a passenger, unless the ATV is designed to carry a passenger.
- At a speed too fast for existing conditions or potential hazards.
- In a careless, reckless or negligent manner.
- While intoxicated or impaired by alcohol or drugs.
- On the tracks or right-of-way of a railroad.
- On a highway, if the ATV is equipped with studded tires other than automobile-type studs.
- In a tree nursery or planting in a manner which damages or destroys growing stock or creates a substantial risk of damage or destruction.
- Within 100 feet of a dwelling between midnight and 6 A.M. at a speed greater than necessary to keep the ATV moving.
- While pulling a person on skis, a toboggan, sleigh, sled or trailer, unless the device is attached to the ATV by a tow-bar or other rigid connection.
- On the ice or public water within 100 feet of a person, fishing shanty or shelter at a speed greater than necessary to keep the ATV moving.
- Over an area cleared of snow for skating, unless necessary for access to public waters.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0018
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
LOCAL LAWS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > LOCAL LAWS]
No locality may require its own ATV licenses or registrations, but it may impose additional restrictions or rules on ATV operation. Find out about special ATV rules in your area, and obey them.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0019
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
SPECIAL EVENTS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > SPECIAL EVENTS]
The person in charge of an ATV special event or off-road competition must apply to the local jurisdiction for written authorization at least 30 days in advance, unless it is held entirely on private property.

chunk_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0::c0020
doc_id: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators#3_0
heading_path: ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators
ATV ACCIDENTS
text:
[ATVs: Information for Owners and Operators > ATV ACCIDENTS]
If you are involved in an accident with your ATV, you must give your name and address, the name and address of the ATV owner and the plate number to injured persons, the owners of damaged property, and/or the police. You also must show proof of insurance to persons claiming to have suffered injury or damage. If property is damaged, and you cannot locate the owner, you must give the above information to police as soon as possible.

You must immediately report to the police any accident that involves death, personal injury or damage estimated at $600 or more to the property of any one person.

You must also file a Report of Motor Vehicle Accident (MV-104) with the Department of Motor Vehicles about an accident that results in a fatality, personal injury, or property damage estimated at $1,000 or more. You must file the report within 10 days of the accident and send a copy to the county sheriff or police commissioner.

If you are incapacitated, the written report may be filed by another party familiar with the accident. The investigating police officer must also file a written report, but that does not relieve you of your legal responsibility to file one.

Failure to report an accident is a misdemeanor. A conviction may result in suspension or revocation of your safety training certificate and/or the ATV registration.

The Department of Motor Vehicles may suspend your safety training certificate and/or the ATV registration until you file an acceptable written report.

Additional information can be found at: Register and title a recreational vehicle (snowmobile, boat, moped or ATV) [9]

NEW YORK STATE DEPARTMENT OF MOTOR VEHICLESMark J. F. Schroeder, Commissioner

Return to DMV Publications [10]

text:
# Automatic license and registration extension for military personnel

Pursuant to Executive Order No. 2 by Governor Andrew M. Cuomo, all licenses and registrations for New York State military personnel returning from active military duty relating to the war on terrorism and military action in Iraq will automatically be extended. The following information will help minimize any potential inconvenience upon their return.

### What happens if my NY State driver license expires while I am on active duty?

NY State law automatically extends license privileges throughout active military service for up to 6 months after discharge or separation. Discharged or separated military personnel may renew an expired NY State license up to two years after the extended expiration. No more than 30 months may have passed since discharge (6-month extension plus 24 -month grace period).

Active military personnel must show proof of date of entry into military service. If the NY State license was valid at any time during your military service, your license can be renewed.

A discharged serviceman must show a Certificate of Discharge, DD-214. You must have been discharged within the past 30 months. If the NY State license was valid at any time during your military service, your license can be renewed.

### Am I required to notify DMV of my entry into the military?

While not required, it is suggested that military personnel file a Notification of Military Service (pdf) [1] (MV -75) to ensure that the license record is not purged once the expiration date has passed.

### What happens if my NY State registration expires while I am on active duty?

Registrations are extended for up to 60 days from return to New York State. This extension applies only to vehicles registered to military personnel. You must show proof of military service or separation. Liability insurance coverage must be maintained at all times, including the period of extension.

### What happens if I had a lapse of insurance coverage during active duty?

You are required to maintain continuous coverage or surrender your plates before deployed. If you were unable to do so, DMV has a procedure in place to exempt you from administrative actions upon your return. You must provide a notarized statement that the vehicle was not used during the time in question, a copy of your military ID, proof of current insurance (or surrender of plates), and signed and dated copies of deployment and return papers, or DD-214 (if separated from service). You can present these documents at any DMV office, or mail them to:

Insurance Services BureauNYS DMV6 Empire State Plaza, Room 332BAlbany, NY 12228

If you have any additional questions, please contact the DMV Call Center [2].

chunk_id: Become a driving school instructor#3_0::c0000
doc_id: Become a driving school instructor#3_0
text:
# Become a driving school instructor

## What is a driving school instructor?

A driving school instructor is a person who has been certified to teach individuals to drive a motor vehicle for a licensed driving school. A certified driving school instructor may be approved to teach in one or more of the following areas

behind-the-wheel instruction in vehicles, including one or more of the following - cars - trucks - buses - tractor-trailers - motorcycles requirements for the Pre-licensing Course [1] (a classroom course)

## What are the requirements to become a driving school instructor?

First, you must be employed by a driving school licensed by DMV. You must also meet several requirements identified in Commissioner s Regulations Part 76.16 [2], including

must be at least 21 years of age must have a driver license valid for operation in New York State that - has been valid for at least 2 years preceding application in the class of vehicle that the instructor intends to teach in, and - has not been suspended or revoked in the last 2 years - shows an acceptable driving record must have a high school or high school equivalency diploma must pass the required tests, which include - a vision test - road sign test - written test - driving school instructor driving test must never have been convicted of a felony or of any crime involving violence, dishonesty, deceit, indecency, degeneracy or moral turpitude

Before your Driving School Instructor Certificate can be renewed, you must also complete a course in driver training and traffic safety, approved by the Commissioner, consisting of at least 30 hours known as the This 30-hour course is taught by various community colleges and driving schools that have been approved by DMV to provide this course.

If you want to teach the Pre-licensing Course [3], you must also successfully complete a 30-hour Teaching Techniques and Methodology course (a college-level course) and have at least one year experience as a behind-the-wheel certified driving school instructor.

## How do I become certified as a driving school instructor?

To become a driving school instructor, you must first be employed by a licensed driving school.

Once you have been hired by a driving school, you must complete an Application for Driving School Instructor Certificate \4\. Be sure to answer all questions, and provide any explanations/information needed. Please include any documentation requested.

Bring your completed application form to the driving school owner. With the application, you will need to include

a copy of your high school or equivalency diploma one passport-type photo of yourself, taken within the last 30 days a check or money order, payable to Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, in the amount of $10. Starter checks, cash, or credit cards cannot be accepted. if your driver license is issued from a state other than New York, you must include with your application a certified copy of your driving record from the state agency that issued your license.

## The driving school owner must mail the application to:

New York State Department of Motor VehiclesBureau of Driver Training Programs6 Empire State Plaza, Room 327Albany, NY 12228(518) 473-7174

Once your application is approved, the Bureau of Driver Training Programs (DTP) will forward your application to the local DMV Testing & Investigations Unit (T&I). The T&I Unit will contact you to schedule your testing 1, which consists of a

## vision test road sign test written test behind-the-wheel instructor s driving test

## A little about the tests you have to pass

The is similar to the vision test you must pass to qualify for, or renew, your driver s license. You can take the vision test at DMV, or you can have your eye doctor or physician conduct this test and complete the Vision Test Report [5] form (MV-619). Attach the Vision Test Report to your application. The evaluates your knowledge of road signs. See the Driver s Manual [6] (MV-21) for more information. The is based on information found in the Driver s Manual [6] (MV-21), Commissioner s Regulations Part 76 [2] (CR-76), and Section 394 of the New York State Vehicle & Traffic Law [7] (MV-299.1). There is a study guide for the Written Test [8], which you can download (MV-368). The will evaluate your ability to drive, and to give a student instruction, in the type of vehicle you want to teach in. You will have to provide your own vehicle for this test.

With each application, you are allowed to take each of the Road Sign Test and Written Test twice, and the Behind-The-Wheel Instructor s Driving Test once. If you do not pass these tests, you will have to submit a new application \4\ including photos and $10 fee.

## About Your Driving School Instructor Certificate (MV-524)

After you pass all tests, the Bureau of Driver Training Programs will issue a Driving School Instructor Certificate (MV-524) and mail it to the driving school where you are employed.

You must carry the Driving School Instructor Certificate whenever you are teaching, and whenever you take a customer to a DMV Road Test Site. If a customer or DMV employee asks to see the certificate, you must be able to present it.

IMPORTANT: The MV-524 only authorizes you to teach for the driving school named on the certificate. Once you are certified as a driving school instructor, you can get an additional certificate naming another school. Simply complete an Application for Driving School Instructor Certificate [4] (form MV-523) and take it to the driving school that has hired you. With the application you will need to include

a copy of your high school or equivalency diploma one passport-type photo of yourself, taken within the last 30 days if your driver license was issued from a state other than New York, you must include a certified copy of your driving record from the state agency that issued your license.

There is no fee for an additional certificate as long as you have a valid certificate with another driving school.

Unless the driving school you are employed by is authorized by DMV to conduct these tests for their employees.

text:
# 买卖车辆（转移所有权）

### 转移所有权

#### 在购买车辆前确定你确切需要什么

使用 DMV 的 Document Guide 确保你从卖方那里获得所有需要的文件，以便在纽约注册你的车辆。

查找你的证明 [1]

#### 一般来说，当转移所有权时...

卖方必须要么

- 填写并签署 title certificate 的转移所有权部分，并且
- 签署 bill of sale [2]（即使是赠与）

要么

- 提供其他可接受的所有权和转移所有权证明 [3]

买方必须

# California emissions standards

### What vehicles are subject to the California emissions standards?

Unless it is exempt, your vehicle must comply with the California emissions standard if it has less than 7,500 miles on the odometer and is

- a model year of 1996 or newer passenger vehicle or light-duty truck that has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 6,000 lbs. or less
- a model year 2000 or newer light-duty truck that has a GVWR of 8,500 lbs. or less
- a model year 2004 or newer medium duty vehicle that has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 14,000 lbs. or less
- a model year 2005 or newer heavy-duty otto-cycle or diesel vehicle that has a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) over 14,000 lbs

### How can I find out if my vehicle meets the California emissions standard?

To determine if a vehicle meets the California emissions standard, look for these words or similar language on the Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin (MCO) and the emissions label under the hood:

- "California-Only Vehicle: This vehicle conforms to U.S. EPA and California regulations applicable to (the vehicle model year) model-year new motor vehicles introduced into commerce only for sale in California."
- "50-State Vehicle: This vehicle conforms to U.S. EPA and California regulations applicable to (the vehicle model year) model-year new motor vehicles."
- "Federal Vehicle certified for Sale in California: This vehicle conforms to U.S. EPA regulations applicable to (the vehicle model year) model-year new motor vehicles, and is certified for sale in California."

### My vehicle complies with the California emissions standard but this is not indicated on the MCO, or I don't have the MCO. What can I do?

If your vehicle complies with the California emissions standard, but the MCO does not indicate compliance or you do not have an Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin (MCO), you or the automobile dealer can certify compliance on a 'Certificate of Emissions Compliance or Exemption' form (MV-74).

If your vehicle is exempt from the California emissions standard, you or the automobile dealer can complete form MV-74 to certify the exemption if

- the vehicle has an odometer reading of more than 7,500 miles, or
- you purchased the vehicle in another state to replace your previous vehicle that was damaged, stolen or had a mechanical failure while you were outside NY State
- the vehicle was transferred to you through an inheritance or court decree
- the vehicle was registered to you in another state when you were a resident of that state, but you are now a resident of NY State
- you are a NY State resident who serves in the US Armed Forces and you are stationed in another state
- the vehicle is an authorized emergency vehicle defined in Article 1 of the NY State Vehicle and Traffic Law

Note: Even if your vehicle meets the California emissions standard, it is subject to NY State safety and emissions inspection requirements.

### Where can I find more information?

The NY State Department of Environmental Conservation website (www.dec.ny.gov [1]) has the regulations for the California emissions standards and other motor vehicle emissions standards (See Regulations, Part 218).

# Changes to IRP registration

# Changes to IRP registration [1]

### Common changes to IRP registrations include

- add or delete vehicles
- transfer plates from one vehicle to another
- add jurisdictions
- increase or decrease registered weight
- transfer a vehicle from one fleet to another fleet
- name change
- address change 1

### To make changes to your IRP registration

- complete Schedule A & C (pdf) [2] (IRP-6) (submit for all changes listed above)
- provide proof of identity (submit for all changes listed above) 2
- provide proof of ownership (submit for all add vehicle requests) 3
- provide proof of NY State insurance (NY State Insurance ID Card) in same name as the registrant if you are adding vehicles to the fleet (submit for all changes listed above)
- provide proof of NY State insurance (NY State Insurance ID Card) in the new name if you are changing the name on the account
- send a check or money order made payable to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles in the amount of $2.50 per vehicle
- send in proof of an established place of business for the new address (submit for for address change only)

### Online

You may use OSCAR [3] to make some of these the changes online.

### By mail

If you are using the United States Postal Service

International Registration BureauPO Box 2850 ESPAlbany, NY 12220-0850

If you use an express mail service or other method

International Registration BureauNYS DMVRoom 1366 Empire State PlazaAlbany, NY 12228

If you send your application by mail, the IRB sends you a invoice. If additional information is required to process your application, the IRB sends a request for additional information with the invoice. Payment by mail must be by certified check or money order.

### At the Customer Service Counter in Albany

You may bring your application to the

Customer Service CounterRoom 136Swan Street BuildingEmpire State PlazaAlbany, NY 12228

The Customer Service Counter is open8:00am to 3:45pm, Monday through Friday, except state holidays

The IRB calculates your fees while you wait. You may pay the fees in cash, by money order or certified check. You must provide payment and all required documents to receive your new IRP documents.

### By fax

Submit the Schedule A & C (pdf) [2] (IRP-6) by fax to 518-486-6579. IRB processes changes submitted by fax within 72 hours.

- 1. If you change your address, you must notify the DMV within 10 days. Please complete Schedule A/C (IRP6) and submit it along with your two proofs of new address and payment in the amount of $2.50 per vehicle. Payment must be a check or money order payable to the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles.
- 2. Send photocopies of your proofs of identity. If another person brings your application to the Customer Service Counter, see the requirements for a second-party registration application.
- 3. If you must change any information on your IRP registration that is also on your title certificate (for example the VIN, year or make), you must first apply for an amendment to your title certificate. See Change name or other information on your registration or title [4] for more information. If you change information on your title certificate, you must send a photocopy of the changed title certificate when you apply to change information on the IRP registration. Your local DMV office cannot amend an IRP registration.

## Do it by phone:

You can't make changes to an IRP registration by phone.

You may call the IRB with questions at 1-518-473-5834

## Do it by mail:

You can make changes to your IRP registrations by mail. Follow the instructions on Schedule A&C [2] (IRP-6).

## Do it at the DMV:

You can make changes to your IRP registrations at the

Customer Service CounterRoom 136Swan Street BuildingEmpire State PlazaAlbany, NY 12228

The Customer Service Counter is open 8:00am to 3:45pm, Monday through Friday, except state holidays

You can't make changes to your IRP registrations at a DMV local office.

## Do it online alternative:

You can make some changes to your IRP registrations using OSCAR [3]

# Commercial Driver License Downgrades

### What must I do if I get a NOTICE OF NON-COMPLIANCE AND LICENSE DOWNGRADE?

If the cause is

You must immediately submit a copy of your USDOT Medical Examiners Certificate to the Medical Certification Unit.

If the cause is

You must immediately submit an updated copy of your USDOT Medical Examiners Certificate to the Medical Certification Unit.

If the cause is

You must contact the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) or your Medical Examiner to have this issue resolved.

You can send the required documents to DMV by mail, fax or e-mail.

Mailing address:

NYS DMVMedical Certification UnitPO Box 2601Albany, NY 12220-0601

Fax: (518) 486-4421 / (518) 486-3260

e-mail: [email protected] [1]

Drivers can monitor their own CLP/CDL medical certification status through MyDMV [2] and subscribe for text and/or email notifications [3].

### What will happen if I don't respond to the NOTICE OF NON-COMPLIANCE AND LICENSE DOWNGRADE?

Failure to respond to the NOTICE OF NON-COMPLIANCE AND LICENSE DOWNGRADE will result in your Commercial Driver License automatically being downgraded to a Non-CDL class and/or your Commercial Learner Permit being cancelled as of the effective date on the notice. We strongly recommend that you submit your required information to the Medical Certification Unit at least 20 days before the effective date of the downgrade. This will allow for receipt and processing time.

If the downgrade/cancellation occurs, your must complete and present an application to reinstate your commercial privileges in person at a DMV office. All normal transaction fees will apply. If you are a Commercial Learner Permit holder, you will need to retake any applicable knowledge tests you passed more than 180 days from the date you apply for reinstatement.

If you no longer want a Commercial Driver License/ Commercial Learner Permit, you can get a non-commercial duplicate license online [4] after the Effective Date on the downgrade notice. The commercial class license document in your possession will no longer be valid.

Note: You may be charged with a violation of the Vehicle and Traffic Law (VTL) if you operate a commercial motor vehicle when

- not medically certified (VTL 509 (7-a))
- not in possession of the appropriate license to operate the vehicle (VTL 509(7), or
- not holding the appropriate class of license to operate the vehicle VTL 509(2)

Sections 509(2) and 509(7) are considered serious disqualifying offenses under federal and state law, when committed in a commercial motor vehicle. If you are convicted of more than one serious , you commercial driver license may be suspended.

# Conditional 和 Restricted Use 许可证

你必须亲自到 DMV 办公室申请 conditional 或 restricted use 许可证。你可以在大多数（但不是所有）Motor Vehicles 办公室办理。请联系离你最近的办公室 [1] 以了解在哪里申请。

### Conditional

DMV 可以向符合条件的驾驶员签发 conditional license，前提是该驾驶员的 NY State 驾照因酒精或毒品相关的违规行为而被吊销或撤销。该驾驶员必须参加由 DMV 批准的 Impaired Driver Program (IDP) [2]（以前称为 Drinking Driving Program (DDP)）。

### Restricted use

DMV 可以向符合条件且其驾照因非酒精或毒品相关的违规或事故，或因某些毒品相关违规而被吊销或撤销的驾驶员签发 restricted use license。

### 来自其他州的驾驶员

如果你持有其他州签发的驾驶执照，并且满足其他要求，你可以获得在 NY State 驾驶的 conditional driving privilege 或 restricted driving privilege。其条件或限制与持有 NY State 驾驶执照的驾驶员相同。

# Creating a MyDMV account

# Creating a MyDMV account [1]

What do I need to sign up for MyDMV?

You must have

- your New York State driver license, permit or non-driver ID 1
- your Social Security Number (SSN)
- the ZIP code currently on your New York State driver license, permit or non-driver ID record 2

How do I sign up for MyDMV?

Step 1: Go to the MyDMV homepage [2] and click "Sign up for MyDMV."

Step 2: Enter the required information and create a NY.gov ID username, or use one your already have. Your information must match what we currently have on for you. 3 Your username can be a combination of

- letters (a,b,c)
- numbers (1,2,3)
- period ( . )
- at ( @ )
- dash ( - )
- underscore ( \_ )

Step 3: Open the email we send you with your temporary password and link to MyDMV.

Step 4: Click the "Log in to NY.gov" button and enter your username and temporary password. 4

Step 5: Create a permanent password and security questions/answers (Shared Secrets). 5

* *Step 6:** Enroll in the MyDMV services you want to use.

What if I already have a NY.gov username?

NY.gov allows people to access online services from various NYS government agencies with a single username. For example, if you have a MyDMV account and you enroll at the Online Tax Center of the Department of Taxation and Finance, you can use the same NY.gov ID username and password to access services offered by both agencies. Learn more about NY.gov ID [3].

If you already have an NY.gov ID username when you sign up for a MyDMV account, your MyDMV account will be associated with your current NY.gov ID username. You will not need to create a new username.

Forgot your NY.gov account Username? Use the self-service tools on the MyDMV homepage [2].

What can I do if I lost my temporary password and couldn't complete the sign-up process?

Follow these steps

* *Step 1:** Go to the MyDMV homepage [2] and click "Sign up here."

Step 2: Enter all the required information again. Use the same username you used before.

Step 3: Open the email we send you with a new temporary password and link to MyDMV to sign in.

Why am I redirected to the 'Register for MyDMV Online Services' page?

You may have multiple NY.gov usernames, and the username you used to sign in is not associated with your MyDMV account. To solve this issue, follow these steps:

Step 1: Use this link to clear out your sign in information from our system [4]. This will stop you from being redirected to the Register for MyDMV Online Services page.

Step 2: Use the Forgot your Username tool on the NY.gov ID sign in page [5] to get a list of all of your NY.gov ID Usernames. If you have more than one email address, be sure to check all of them. Sign in with the username you created for MyDMV. If you don't remember the password you can use the 'Forgot your Password' tool.

None of these instructions help. I still can't sign up for MyDMV.

If you still have problems signing up after following the instructions on this page, Contact us [6].

- 1. If you just ordered a new driver license, learner permit, or non-driver ID but it hasn t arrived in the mail, you ll need to wait until you receive your new document to create your account.You **cannot** create a MyDMV account if you were never issued a New York State license, permit, or non-driver ID.
- 2. You can confirm or change your address online [7]
- 3. Make sure you enter your photo document number correctly (see a sample driver license [8]). It s easy to mistake the following
  - the number 1 for letter the I
  - the number 0 for the letter O
  - the letter Q and the letter O
  - the number 5 and the letter S
  - the number '8' and the letter 'B'
- 4. The temporary password is case sensitive. You must enter it exactly as it appears in the email. It is best to copy and paste the temporary password from the email.
- 5. Your password must
  - be different from your temporary password and username
  - contain at least 8 characters
  - include at least one upper case and one lower case character
  - be different from your previous 12 passwords
